The ability to change the settings are endless and was fun to play with. What I like is these are bright enough to be used to illuminate a work bench or a working area, and also as decorative lighting like I am going to use them for. These LED lights are more than I had hoped for and are amazing for the price. They are on a strip which you can cut to length and is adhesive backed. I will be using some extra strength double sided tape to help hold it in place. If you need LED strip lighting for indoor use, this is definitely something you can use and able to do more than people think! My son wants some now for his room to put up. As you can see from the last photo I decided to install them in my new office. I used the adhesive backing on the strip and it stuck no problem. I cut to the length of the space I had and it worked fantastic! I get a lot of compliments.

Lost my original Minn Kota fob overboard last season and finally pulled the trigger on this replacement. Ordered it on a Monday and it was at my door by Wednesday afternoon, nicely packed in a sturdy box with plenty of padding so it wasn't rattling around. Feels identical to the factory remote that came with my Terrova. Solid little unit, good weight to it, buttons have a nice tactile click. Paired it up in about ten seconds, no fuss at all. Range seems just as good as the original. Comes with the lanyard and battery already installed, which was a pleasant surprise. Honestly can't tell any difference between this and the one that shipped with the motor brand new. Great value compared to buying direct from the dealer.

Bought this heater thinking it would handle our drafty sunroom through the winter. Right out of the box it seemed decent enough, put out solid heat for about three months. Then it started doing this weird thing where it would shut off randomly mid-cycle and the thermostat clearly wasn't reading the room temperature correctly anymore. By month four it barely warmed anything and just made a faint clicking sound every time I turned it on. Reached out to the seller and never heard back. Ended up tossing it and buying something from an actual hardware store instead. Save yourself the headache and spend a little more on a unit that'll actually last more than a single season. Total waste of money.
Not what I hoped for. The color looks really unnatural in person, nothing like the warm tone shown online. Ended up returning them because they just looked cheap.

I purchased this as a quiet learning activity for my 2.5-year-old and have not been disappointed. I read another review saying it's not for an 18 month or 2 year old and I agree with that... It's simply not durable enough for those littler ones as the stickers are vinyl and the backgrounds are a thicker cardstock; however, we have had no issues with my 2.5-year-old ripping the backgrounds or having trouble with the stickers. Its proving to be a great learning activity as every time she pulls off a sticker she tells me what it is or asks if she didn't know. It helps them associate what animals belong to which habitat in addition to learning what the habitats themselves are. Our stickers have stuck great though you have to be kind of careful when taking them off and moving them to a new spot as they get bent from finger nails fairly easily. Overall we are really happy with this and my toddler loves it which is what matters most!

Some sections drag a bit with background info but the personal stuff is super compelling. For the price of a coffee you get a really eye-opening look inside a world most people never see. Glad I picked it up.

Great quality pellets at a fair price. My two piggies gobble these up every single morning.

These have been my primary tennis shoes for about 3 months. The style is nice, but they just aren't going to work for me long term. PROs: - Great for plantar fascitiis - Stylish - Can remove insole and use custom orthotics. - Great for walking CONs: - Expensive - Odd sizing. I normally wear a size 8 or size 8W. I needed to replace all the ancient detectors in the home we just bought, and these seemed like the best bet. The thing I really appreciate is the front-loading battery compartment. Our old ones required twisting the whole unit off the mounting bracket to swap batteries, which usually meant the plastic tabs broke. With this model, you just pop the front cover open while it's still secured to the ceiling. Took me maybe thirty seconds per unit to get them powered up and tested. The dual sensor gives me serious peace of mind too since we have a fireplace and I worry about both fast flames and slow smoldering. Loud alert, clean look, and the battery design alone makes it worth every penny.

Ordered this ebook last night and it downloaded to my Paperwhite instantly, no hiccups at all. The cover art pulled me in right away and the formatting is clean, no weird spacing or typos like some indie titles. Started reading during my lunch break and honestly did not want to put it down. The worldbuilding hits hard, a brutal drought society run by some power-hungry governor. The characters feel like real people making tough calls in an impossible situation. I am about forty percent through and already invested in what happens next. For the price this is a steal. If you like post-apocalyptic stuff with political intrigue baked in, grab this one. Hoping the author drops a sequel soon because I will be first in line.

Although Daniel Craig isn't my favorite Bond, this movie is well worth watching. Strong script, good acting, and excellent action make for an enjoyable 2hr 24min film. My favorite part is the blast from the past in the last quarter of the movie... No spoilers here, but you'll know it when you see it! Great way to spend an evening! Highly recommended...
Installed these on my son's mountain bike over a year ago. They've survived crashes, mud, and daily rides to school. Still shifting crisp and smooth. Excellent quality for the price.

Got this on a Kindle deal for 99 cents and honestly that's about what it's worth. The whole quest to track down that magical buckle thing felt pretty generic, like I've read this same basic plot a dozen times before. The fantasy worlds themselves are actually pretty cool and vividly drawn, I'll give it that much. But the pacing drags badly in the middle section and I found myself skimming whole chapters. Characters are okay but nobody really stood out or felt memorable. At full price I'd probably be more annoyed, but for a buck it passed the time on my commute. If you're deep into the series already might as well grab it, but I wouldn't go out of my way. Decent enough bargain bin fantasy.

Native Son hit me harder than I expected. The thing I kept coming back to is how Wright puts you inside Bigger's head, the paranoia, the racing thoughts, the way he processes fear. That psychological depth is what makes this worth reading. Some of the pacing drags in the middle section, and Max's courtroom speech runs way too long. I caught myself skimming. But the opening chapters are incredibly tense and well constructed. The cat-and-mouse tension after the first incident had me completely hooked. My used paperback had some highlighting from a previous owner which was mildly annoying, but the print quality was fine. Took me about a week to get through. Not a light read by any means, but an important one that sticks with you afterward.

I read this book as a teen-ager and was constantly putting it down because it was making me so nervous. I saw even then, at a young age, how possible it was for this world to become a reality. How many people try to lose themselves in drugs, alcohol, meaningless TV? We are closer to this Brave New World than we like to admit. Can this insanity our world is headed toward be stopped? I don't know but I fear that Huxley understood the human conditon all too well. We believe everything we hear on TV or read in the newspapers. Too many of us have left our intelligence and perception at the door. Wake up before it is too late and think for yourself. There was a version of Brave New World with Leonard Nimoy which presented a sort of happy ending for two people, which did not occur in the book but still leaves the Brave New World untouched. I won't say too much about John "the Savage" who was more human than the rest of the population but he is the mirror Huxley uses to show us how barren and sterile this Brave New World is. A place where every word can be uttered except mother and father. Children are born in laboratories. The family unit has been disassembled with all loyalty going to the state. As frightening as it is, it a must read for those who want to understand what is happening now and how easily it can happen. The question becomes: do we rule technology or do we allow it to rule us?
